evidence.note: Four stories (lead, microsoft-ai-chip-gap, anthropic-credit-facility, chatgpt-for-teens) rely on a tier-1/tier-2 primary that returned 403 to a direct fetch — Anthropic's PDF, the Guardian, Bloomberg and OpenAI. Each was handled under the rubric's blocked-primary rule: a source actually opened quotes the primary directly, confidence is capped at medium, and the prose attributes the claim to the reporting read rather than the document itself. chatgpt-for-teens was upgraded post-scoring from a tier-4 secondary (Tech Startups) to TechCrunch (tier 2, Sarah Perez byline, directly fetched), which also supplied a genuine counterpoint — the safeguards arrive years after ChatGPT scaled to 900 million weekly users with no teen mode. Correct handling throughout, but the four blocked-primary cases still cost a point rather than a clean 5.

Every figure carries a basis — e.g. the Anthropic credit story states "$2.5 billion five-year revolving credit line Anthropic arranged in 2025" as the comparison point for the new $10bn target, and the Cerebras story explicitly separates the vendor's "up to 30 times" claim from The Register's finding that the doubled figure comes from a higher clock speed on the same transistor count.

Bullets read as facts throughout — the lead's third bullet is "The report also discloses an internal model, Model 2, that improves on Mythos 5 on many internal tasks but has no plans for external release," not a topic label. Docked from 5 only because a few whyItMatters paragraphs (microsoft-ai-chip-gap, chatgpt-for-teens) run long, multi-clause sentences that could be split.

The lead (Anthropic's own risk-rating change and an unreleased, more-capable model) is well-argued but not unarguable — Pennsylvania's data-center order or the Microsoft chip-count investigation could each defend the slot instead. No sub-$10m funding rounds or unchecked vendor-benchmark leads made it in; Cerebras's headline number is paired with independent scrutiny rather than run as fact.

Models lands one story against a quota of three; edition.summary says so directly ("Models coverage stays thin today — nothing genuinely new cleared the bar beyond a Google API deprecation") after a genuine search that found nothing else in the last 48 hours not already covered in Nos. 1-2. No company exceeds 2 of 12 stories (Anthropic: risk report + credit facility, on unrelated news).
